Definition: from G1849; to control:--exercise authority upon, bring under the (have) power of.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, exousiázō is the word for exercise authority upon, bring under the (have) power of. In Luke 22:25, the text says "The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them." In 1 Corinthians 6:12, the text says "but I will not be brought under the power of any."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading exousiázō this way, I believe authority belongs to God first; every other authority answers to His. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
